question: Does a visual inspection of official JICA-hosted Table 2.15 resolve whether its four common-name nekton labels are assigned to one river or shared across both rows?

sourceReinspection.document: Department of Transportation and Communications. (2015). Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan (EPRMP) for the North South Commuter Rail (NSCR) Project, Volume I: Main Report, Draft, March 2015.
sourceReinspection.retrieval: The official JICA-hosted 233-page PDF was downloaded to a temporary local review directory, not retained in the repository.

locator.table: Table 2.15 Biological Components of Guiguinto and Meycauayan Rivers

visualTableCheck.finding: The River and Macroinvertebrates columns have separate Guiguinto and Meycauyan rows. The Nekton column is one vertically merged cell spanning both rows; its four bullets are Giant mottled eel, Catfish, Tilapia, and Mudfish/Striped snakehead.
visualTableCheck.interpretation: The table supports only a shared Guiguinto-Meycauyan historical common-name lead. It does not assign any listed label to one river, station, date, or specimen.
visualTableCheck.textCrosscheck: The publisher text extraction lists the four bullets after the Guiguinto row and before the Meycauyan row. The page image resolves the layout: the Nekton cell spans both river rows, while the Macroinvertebrates cells are row-specific (Chironomidae at Guiguinto; None at Meycauyan).
visualTableCheck.reconcilesReview: Confirms the shared-cell interpretation in the 2026-11-20 review and replaces its then-open visual-layout check.

unchangedEvidenceLimits.taxonomy: All four entries remain common-name categories; no scientific-name mapping or specimen identification is established.
unchangedEvidenceLimits.sampling: The report section supplies no fish-specific method, field date, count, effort, or voucher. The March 2015 cover date is not a fish collection date.
unchangedEvidenceLimits.reuse: No item-specific open-data license or permission to reproduce the table or redistribute its content was verified.
unchangedEvidenceLimits.currentStatus: The draft EPRMP is historical project evidence, not a current occurrence, abundance, catchability, access, safety, or legal-harvest assessment.

nextActions: Keep the four labels as attributed shared river-system research leads until an independent primary source resolves taxonomy, fish-specific sampling, date, and site assignment.
Continue Central Luzon freshwater source review; the visual table check does not close Bulacan river coverage or the regional baseline.

sources.supports: Official JICA-hosted March 2015 draft DOTC EPRMP, including the visually reviewed Table 2.15 on printed page 96 and its shared merged Nekton cell.
